attrs.claim: Public API stubs and feature examples: Update the `.pyi` type stubs whenever public APIs are added or changed. Demonstrate new features in `docs/examples.md`.

Docstring summary mood and return section: Write docstring summary lines in imperative mood; the rest of the docstring explains behavior and need not use imperative mood. Label the return-value section `Returns:`.
Type stub notation and import suggestions: Use modern type notation in type stubs and preserve their organization so VS Code's quick-fix import suggestions prefer the attrs namespace.
Namedtuple serialization with retained collection types: attr.asdict supports namedtuple fields when retain_collection_types=True, preserving their namedtuple type.

Preserve legacy attr.ib references in documentation: When documenting attrs.field, retain references to attr.ib where they help readers navigate older attrs code; attrs.field may appear first. Do not refer to attrs.ib, which does not exist.

API documentation registration and version directives: Manually add new functions/classes and signature changes to `@attr.s()` and `@attrs.define()` to `docs/api.rst`. Give changed or added classes, methods, and functions appropriate `versionadded`, `versionchanged`, or `deprecated` directives; changes affecting both `attrs.define()` and `attr.s()` require directives on both.
Multiline docstring layout: In `src/attr/_make.py`, put opening and closing docstring quotes on separate lines, even for a one-sentence docstring.
Semantic newlines in documentation: Write `.rst` and `.md` documentation using semantic newlines, with one sentence per line.

Canonical Python version: The root `.python-version` file is the canonical source for the project's default Python version, including for setup-python. Use its version when creating a development virtual environment.

Test assertions and feature strategies: Write assertions as `expected == actual`, with an empty line before the assertion block, and give tests descriptive docstrings. Add new features to the Hypothesis testing strategy in `tests/strategies.py`.
Required tests, documentation, and coverage: Always include tests and documentation for code changes; CI requires 100% coverage. Use `# pragma: no cover` only when maintainers agree to an exception.
Boolean references in API docstrings: Use Sphinx roles :data:`True` and :data:`False` when referring to boolean literals in API docstrings.

Towncrier changelog fragments and symbol formatting: For user-facing changes, add a Markdown fragment under changelog.d named pr#.(change|deprecation|breaking).md, using semantic newlines and simple past tense or constructions with “now”. Format fully qualified symbols in plain backticks; Sphinx roles such as {func} do not work in changelog fragments.

Public API compatibility policy: Announce compatibility breaks in the changelog and, where possible, issue a `DeprecationWarning` for a year before breaking compatibility. The structure of `attrs.Attribute` is exempt from this guarantee and should be treated as read-only.

rich.claim: Preserve Traceback serialization and captured state: Keep Traceback trivially serializable; avoid retaining arbitrary renderables that compromise serialization or whose mutable state could become outdated before printing.
FORCE_COLOR presence forces terminal mode: In terminal detection, any defined FORCE_COLOR value, including an empty string, sets `_force_terminal` to True.
Use safe representations in exception handling: Use `safe_repr` when obtaining object representations during traceback processing; direct `__repr__` calls can raise exceptions or return non-strings.

Poetry development environment: Rich uses Poetry for packaging and dependency management; enter the project's isolated environment with `poetry shell` and install dependencies with `poetry install`. Run the contribution guide's development commands inside that environment.

Preserve named tuple edge cases and custom representations: Named tuple detection must support tuple subclasses and accept an empty tuple for _fields. When pretty-printing named tuples, respect an overridden __repr__ instead of applying default named tuple formatting.
Avoid abbreviated names: Rich has a strict policy against abbreviations in names; use descriptive names instead of names such as `x` or `s`.

Preserve the module-based diagnostics command: Keep python -m rich.diagnose as the command in bug-report instructions. Invoke report() from the module's __main__ block so this command provides the same diagnostic information.

Inspect rendered objects defensively: In pretty rendering, do not assume objects have `__class__` or `__module__`; use defensive `getattr` access. Do not derive qualified class names by slicing `str(class_)`, since that representation is unreliable.

Use JSON-specific whitespace in highlighting: When scanning whitespace in JSON highlighting, accept only whitespace permitted by the JSON specification rather than all characters in string.whitespace.

Resolve Jupyter dimensions only when needed: Look up JUPYTER_COLUMNS only when width is unset, using an explicit `if not width` guard. Keep Jupyter default dimensions in module-level constants, including JUPYTER_DEFAULT_COLUMNS = 115.
Document parameters of private Windows console wrappers: Document every parameter of the Windows console wrapper methods, including private methods.

Demo content affects tests and screenshots: The example content in rich/__main__.py is used by tests and screenshots. When changing that content, account for affected tests and regenerate the screenshots.

Document user-facing changes and build documentation: Consider updating documentation in `docs` for changes with user impact. Install documentation dependencies by running `pip install -r requirements.txt` from `docs`, then run `make docs` from the project root to generate HTML at `docs/build/html`.
Completed progress has zero remaining time: When a progress task has zero remaining work, its remaining-time estimate should return 0 rather than None.

Traceback control locals use truthiness: Evaluate `_rich_traceback_omit` and `_rich_traceback_guard` by their values, defaulting to False when absent. Their presence alone should not trigger traceback control behavior.

echo.claim: Context parameter ordering in middleware: When adding echo.Context to function types or fields, make it the first parameter for consistent signatures.

Middleware configuration and error handling: Do not panic on invalid configuration in middleware creator functions; provide configuration structs implementing MiddlewareConfigurator so callers can choose panic-based or error-returning creation. Request-handling middleware should return errors rather than call c.Error() and return no error, so upstream middleware can handle returned errors.

libuv.claim: Shared I/O transfer limit: Use UV__IO_MAX_BYTES (0x7ffff000) as the shared limit for read and write transfers to avoid platform-specific failures with large requests.
Filesystem polling paths are dynamically allocated: uv_fs_poll_start dynamically allocates its path storage. Do not impose a UV__PATH_MAX limit on that path.
Windows pipe IOCP completion requirements: Windows pipe servers require IOCP to avoid deadlock. Do not enqueue requests in pending_reqs when they will complete via IOCP.

Platform-dependent IPv6 address buffer size: Use INET6_ADDRSTRLEN for the address buffer in uv_ip6_addr. POSIX requires 46 bytes including the NUL byte; Windows requires 65 bytes to accommodate optional formatting marks.
Prefer uv_open_osfhandle: Use uv_open_osfhandle instead of _open_osfhandle when converting Windows OS handles to file descriptors, including in tests.

Cached process IDs can identify a different process: Calling uv_kill with a cached value of uv_process_get_pid can kill a different process that reused the PID after the original process exited. Do not rely on that combination to target only the original process.
Group Windows-only test declarations: Place Windows-only test declarations in the existing Windows-only tests section of test/test-list.h.

Thread pool request classification: Do not use a NULL work callback to identify requests outside the thread pool: worker() clears req->work concurrently when processing finishes. Use the done callback for this distinction because it is never modified and is never NULL for requests that go through the thread pool.
Closing handles does not impose ordering: Do not rely on uv_close to impose an ordering between handle closures, including on Windows.
Reserve handle data for applications: Do not use a handle's public data pointer to store libuv internal state; it is reserved for application use.
Constant-time queue concatenation: Use uv__queue_add to append an entire queue to another queue in O(1), avoiding an O(n) loop that removes and reinserts each entry.

Use the completed Windows pipe I/O result: Determine Windows pipe I/O success from the I/O operation's result rather than the result of CancelIoEx. An ERROR_OPERATION_ABORTED result with bytes > 0 indicates that data was successfully transferred.

Dedicated async handle tracking: src/unix/async.c maintains a dedicated loop->async_handles queue to avoid scanning unrelated handles. Use dedicated async-handle tracking for similar traversal in src/win/async.c, where scanning all handles can be slow.

Cancellation success promises future completion: Returning zero from uv_cancel means the request will complete in the future, allowing the caller to determine when its memory can be released. If a closing handle prevents that completion, return UV_EBUSY or another error instead.

Preserve the Windows global job object during cleanup: Leave the global job object open when cleaning up libuv on Windows. Closing it terminates every process still assigned to it, which should happen when the process exits rather than when it stops using libuv.

import pytest

from attr.validators import deep_iterable, deep_mapping


@pytest.mark.parametrize("sequence_type", [list, tuple])
@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("factory", "argument", "value", "expected"),
    [
        (deep_iterable, "member_validator", [1], 1),
        (deep_iterable, "iterable_validator", [1], [1]),
        (deep_mapping, "key_validator", {"a": 1}, "a"),
        (deep_mapping, "value_validator", {"a": 1}, 1),
        (deep_mapping, "mapping_validator", {"a": 1}, {"a": 1}),
    ],
)
def test_validator_sequences(sequence_type, factory, argument, value, expected):
    calls = []
    instance = object()
    attribute = object()

    def first(inst, attr, item):
        calls.append(("first", inst, attr, item))

    def second(inst, attr, item):
        calls.append(("second", inst, attr, item))

    def noop(inst, attr, item):
        pass

    kwargs = {"member_validator": noop} if factory is deep_iterable else {
        "key_validator": noop
    }
    kwargs[argument] = sequence_type([first, second])
    validator = factory(**kwargs)

    validator(instance, attribute, value)
    assert calls == [
        ("first", instance, attribute, expected),
        ("second", instance, attribute, expected),
    ]

    calls.clear()
    error = ValueError("validation failed")

    def fail(inst, attr, item):
        raise error

    kwargs[argument] = sequence_type([fail, second])
    validator = factory(**kwargs)
    with pytest.raises(ValueError) as exc_info:
        validator(instance, attribute, value)
    assert exc_info.value is error
    assert calls == []

    kwargs[argument] = sequence_type()
    factory(**kwargs)(instance, attribute, value)

    kwargs[argument] = sequence_type([None])
    with pytest.raises(TypeError):
        factory(**kwargs)


@pytest.mark.parametrize("sequence_type", [list, tuple])
def test_mapping_sequences_preserve_optional_validators(sequence_type):
    calls = []

    def record(inst, attr, value):
        calls.append(value)

    deep_mapping(key_validator=sequence_type([record]))(
        None, None, {"a": 1}
    )
    assert calls == ["a"]

    calls.clear()
    deep_mapping(value_validator=sequence_type([record]))(
        None, None, {"a": 1}
    )
    assert calls == [1]

    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        deep_mapping(mapping_validator=sequence_type([record]))

import sys
import typing

import pytest

import attr
import attrs


pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(
    sys.version_info < (3, 14),
    reason="Requires Python 3.14's deferred annotations",
)


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "decorate",
    [attr.s(auto_attribs=True), attrs.define, attrs.frozen],
)
def test_forward_references(decorate):
    """
    Deferred annotations allow forward references that can later be resolved.
    """
    from annotationlib import ForwardRef

    @decorate
    class A:
        b: B  # noqa: F821
        children: list[B]  # noqa: F821
        count: typing.ClassVar[int] = 0

    assert ["b", "children"] == [a.name for a in attrs.fields(A)]
    assert isinstance(attrs.fields(A).b.type, ForwardRef)
    assert isinstance(
        typing.get_args(attrs.fields(A).children.type)[0], ForwardRef
    )

    @decorate
    class B:
        a: A

    attrs.resolve_types(A, globals(), locals())
    attrs.resolve_types(B, globals(), locals())

    assert attrs.fields(A).b.type is B
    assert attrs.fields(A).children.type == list[B]
    assert attrs.fields(B).a.type is A

    b = B(None)
    a = A(b, [b])

    assert a.b is b
    assert a.children == [b]
    assert a.count == 0

# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT

import sys
import typing

import pytest

import attr
import attrs


pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(
    sys.version_info < (3, 14),
    reason="Requires Python 3.14 deferred annotations",
)


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "decorator",
    [attr.s(auto_attribs=True), attrs.define, attrs.frozen],
)
def test_forward_references(decorator, slots):
    """
    Allow unresolved annotations and resolve them once their types exist.
    """

    @decorator(slots=slots)
    class A:
        b: B  # noqa: F821
        bs: list[B]  # noqa: F821
        count: int

    fields = attr.fields(A)

    assert isinstance(fields.b.type, typing.ForwardRef)
    assert "B" == fields.b.type.__forward_arg__
    assert isinstance(fields.bs.type.__args__[0], typing.ForwardRef)
    assert "B" == fields.bs.type.__args__[0].__forward_arg__
    assert int == fields.count.type

    @decorator(slots=slots)
    class B:
        a: A

    attr.resolve_types(A, globals(), locals())
    attr.resolve_types(B, globals(), locals())

On Python 3.14, attrs now supports deferred annotations containing unresolved forward references while preserving annotations whose types are already defined.
Forward references can be resolved using ``attrs.resolve_types()`` once the referenced types are defined.

# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT

import sys
import typing

import pytest

import attr
import attrs


pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(
    sys.version_info < (3, 14),
    reason="Requires Python 3.14 deferred annotations",
)


@pytest.mark.parametrize("decorator", [attr.s, attrs.define])
def test_forward_references(decorator, slots):
    """
    Deferred annotations preserve forward references until types are resolved.
    """

    @decorator(slots=slots, auto_attribs=True)
    class A:
        direct: B
        nested: list[B]
        value: int
        ignored: typing.ClassVar[int] = 42

    fields = attr.fields(A)
    instance = A(None, [], 1)

    assert ("direct", "nested", "value") == tuple(
        field.name for field in fields
    )
    assert isinstance(fields.direct.type, typing.ForwardRef)
    assert "B" == fields.direct.type.__forward_arg__
    assert list == typing.get_origin(fields.nested.type)
    assert isinstance(
        typing.get_args(fields.nested.type)[0], typing.ForwardRef
    )
    assert int == fields.value.type
    assert 1 == instance.value

    @decorator(slots=slots, auto_attribs=True)
    class B:
        value: int

    attr.resolve_types(A, globals(), locals())
    fields = attr.fields(A)
    instance = A(B(2), [B(3)], 1)

    assert B == fields.direct.type
    assert list[B] == fields.nested.type
    assert int == fields.value.type
    assert B(2) == instance.direct
    assert [B(3)] == instance.nested

import pytest

import attr


@pytest.mark.parametrize("collection_type", [list, tuple, set, frozenset])
@pytest.mark.parametrize("retain", [False, True])
def test_recursive_collection_conversion(collection_type, retain):
    """
    Collection conversion preserves the requested type and converts children.
    """
    child_type = attr.make_class("Child", ["value"], frozen=True)
    parent_type = attr.make_class("Parent", ["children"])
    inst = parent_type(collection_type([child_type(1)]))

    (result,) = attr.astuple(inst, retain_collection_types=retain)

    expected_type = collection_type if retain else list
    assert type(result) is expected_type
    assert result == expected_type([(1,)])


def test_retained_namedtuple():
    """
    Retained named tuples still support positional construction.
    """
    pair_type = namedtuple("Pair", ["left", "right"])
    child_type = attr.make_class("Child", ["value"])
    parent_type = attr.make_class("Parent", ["pair"])
    inst = parent_type(pair_type(child_type(1), child_type(2)))

    (result,) = attr.astuple(inst, retain_collection_types=True)

    assert type(result) is pair_type
    assert result == pair_type((1,), (2,))


@pytest.mark.parametrize("recurse", [False, None, 1])
def test_nonrecursive_custom_factory(recurse):
    """
    Nonrecursive conversion passes a list to custom factories and retains values.
    """
    child_type = attr.make_class("Child", ["value"])
    parent_type = attr.make_class("Parent", ["child"])
    child = child_type(1)
    calls = []

    def factory(values):
        calls.append(values)
        return tuple(values)

    result = attr.astuple(
        parent_type(child), recurse=recurse, tuple_factory=factory
    )

    assert result[0] is child
    assert len(calls) == 1
    assert type(calls[0]) is list
    assert calls[0][0] is child

"""Regression tests for astuple's optimized conversion paths."""

from collections import namedtuple

import pytest

from attr import astuple, ib, s


@s
class Container:
    """An attrs class containing an arbitrary value."""

    value = ib()


@pytest.mark.parametrize("recurse", [False, None, 0])
@pytest.mark.parametrize("factory", [tuple, list])
def test_shallow_conversion(recurse, factory):
    """Shallow conversion preserves nested values and honors the factory."""
    nested = Container(1)

    result = astuple(
        Container(nested), recurse=recurse, tuple_factory=factory
    )

    assert type(result) is factory
    assert result[0] is nested


def test_shallow_custom_factory():
    """Custom factories continue to receive a list of field values."""
    calls = []

    def factory(values):
        assert type(values) is list
        calls.append(values)
        return tuple(values)

    assert astuple(Container(1), recurse=False, tuple_factory=factory) == (1,)
    assert calls == [[1]]


def test_shallow_filter():
    """Filtering still runs when recursion is disabled."""
    calls = []

    def exclude(attribute, value):
        calls.append((attribute.name, value))
        return False

    assert astuple(Container(1), recurse=False, filter=exclude) == ()
    assert calls == [("value", 1)]


@pytest.mark.parametrize("collection_type", [list, tuple])
@pytest.mark.parametrize("retain", [False, True])
def test_recursive_collection(collection_type, retain):
    """Collection conversion preserves recursion and retention semantics."""
    values = collection_type([Container(1), Container(2)])

    (result,) = astuple(
        Container(values), retain_collection_types=retain
    )

    expected_type = collection_type if retain else list
    assert type(result) is expected_type
    assert result == expected_type([(1,), (2,)])
    assert result is not values


def test_retained_namedtuple():
    """Retained namedtuples still use positional construction when needed."""
    pair = namedtuple("Pair", ["left", "right"])

    (result,) = astuple(
        Container(pair(Container(1), Container(2))),
        retain_collection_types=True,
    )

    assert type(result) is pair
    assert result == pair((1,), (2,))

"""Regression tests for tuple conversion optimizations."""

import pytest

import attr
import attrs


@pytest.mark.parametrize("recurse", [False, None, 0, 1])
def test_nonrecursive_factory_input(recurse):
    """Custom factories receive a list containing the original values."""
    cls = attr.make_class("Example", ["value"])
    nested = cls(1)
    instance = cls(nested)
    received = []

    def factory(values):
        received.append(values)
        return tuple(values)

    result = attr.astuple(
        instance, recurse=recurse, tuple_factory=factory
    )

    assert result == (nested,)
    assert result[0] is nested
    assert len(received) == 1
    assert type(received[0]) is list


@pytest.mark.parametrize("convert", [attr.astuple, attrs.astuple])
@pytest.mark.parametrize("factory", [tuple, list, set, frozenset])
def test_collection_conversion(convert, factory):
    """Collection conversion preserves values and copies mutable inputs."""
    cls = attr.make_class("Example", ["value"])
    original = factory([1, 2])

    result = convert(cls(original))[0]

    expected_type = list if convert is attr.astuple else factory
    assert type(result) is expected_type
    assert set(result) == {1, 2}
    if isinstance(original, (list, set)):
        assert result is not original


def test_retained_list_subclass():
    """Retained list subclasses still run their constructors."""
    class CustomList(list):
        """A list subclass retained during conversion."""

    cls = attr.make_class("Example", ["value"])
    original = CustomList([1, 2])

    result = attr.astuple(
        cls(original), retain_collection_types=True
    )[0]

    assert type(result) is CustomList
    assert result == original
    assert result is not original

`attr.astuple()` now avoids redundant list copies when converting collections.
Nonrecursive conversions without a filter now collect attribute values more efficiently.

Add alongside the field-transformer explanation:

Field aliases are resolved before `field_transformer` is called, so every
input attribute has an alias. The default alias is the field name with
leading underscores removed. To recognize this default, compare

the same value is indistinguishable from the default.

Calling `Attribute.evolve(name=...)` also updates an alias that matches the
default for the old name. Other aliases are preserved, and passing `alias`
explicitly to `evolve()` takes precedence. Attributes added by a transformer
with `alias=None` receive their default aliases after transformation.

Field aliases are resolved before `field_transformer` is called.
The default alias is the field name with leading underscores removed.
Transformers can detect this default using
`field.alias == field.name.lstrip("_")`.
An explicitly supplied alias equal to the default is indistinguishable from an automatically generated alias.
Fields added by a transformer have their missing aliases resolved afterward.

Calling `Attribute.evolve(name=...)` also updates the alias when it matches the default for the old name, unless an `alias` argument is supplied.
Other explicit aliases are preserved.

```pycon
>>> def keep_underscores(cls, fields):
...     return [
...         field.evolve(alias=field.name)
...         if field.alias == field.name.lstrip("_")
...         else field
...         for field in fields
...     ]
>>> @attrs.define(field_transformer=keep_underscores)
... class Example:
...     _value: int
...     _other: int = attrs.field(alias="custom")
>>> example = Example(_value=1, custom=2)
>>> (example._value, example._other)
(1, 2)
```

Transformers that checked for `alias is None` to detect default aliases must now compare `alias` with `name.lstrip("_")`.
Missing aliases on fields added by a transformer are resolved afterward.

`attrs.Attribute.evolve()` now updates the alias when the name changes and the existing alias matches the default for the old name, unless an alias is explicitly supplied to `evolve()`.

    args = (instance, "value", 2) if operation is setattr else (

def test_frozen_attribute_message():

        value = attr.ib()

    instance = FrozenAttribute(1)

    with pytest.raises(FrozenAttributeError) as exc_info:
        instance.value = 2

    assert exc_info.value.args == ("can't set attribute",)
    assert str(exc_info.value) == "can't set attribute"

It receives the value to convert and returns the converted value.
Defining it inside the class does not add a `self` argument.

A field's converter can be defined next to the field using a decorator:

```{doctest}
>>> from attrs import define, field

>>> @define
... class Measurement:
...     value: float = field()
...
...     @value.converter
...     def convert_value(value):
...         return float(value.strip())

>>> Measurement(" 3.5 ")
Measurement(value=3.5)
```

that field's converter and returns the callable unchanged. Its calling
convention is identical to a callable passed using ``converter=``.
Converters can now be registered using a field's `@field.converter` decorator, alongside the existing `converter=` argument.

def test_assoc_defers_copy_import():
    """
    Introspection leaves copy deferred until assoc needs it.

    subprocess.run(

                original_import = builtins.__import__
                copy_imports = []

                def track_import(name, globals=None, locals=None,
                                 fromlist=(), level=0):
                    if (

# Add before pipe(). Detection is local to construction of a setter or class,
# so cached results do not retain user hooks indefinitely.
class _GeneratorDetector:
    """
    Detect generator functions, importing inspect only when needed.
    """

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self._check = None
        self._cache: dict[int, tuple[object, bool]] = {}

    def __call__(self, hook: object) -> bool:
        # The default pipeline must not cause inspect to be imported.
        if hook is convert or hook is validate or hook is frozen:
            return False

        # Pipelines already know whether they are generator functions.
        pipeline_result = getattr(
            hook, "__attrs_setter_is_generator__", None
        )
        if pipeline_result is not None:
            return pipeline_result

        cached = self._cache.get(id(hook))
        if cached is not None:
            return cached[1]

        if self._check is None:
            from inspect import isgeneratorfunction

            self._check = isgeneratorfunction

        result = self._check(hook)
        # Retain the object alongside its id to prevent id reuse. This also
        # supports callable objects that are unhashable.
        self._cache[id(hook)] = hook, result
        return result


# Replace pipe().
def pipe(*setters):
    """
    Run all *setters* and return the return value of the last one.

    Generator functions must yield exactly once. Their yielded values are
    passed to the next setter. After the final value is assigned, generators
    resume in reverse order.

    If a subsequent setter or the assignment raises an exception, it is thrown
    into the active generators, following the context manager protocol.

    .. versionadded:: 20.1.0
    """
    is_generator = _GeneratorDetector()
    generator_flags = [is_generator(setter) for setter in setters]

    if any(generator_flags):
        from contextlib import ExitStack, contextmanager

        prepared = tuple(
            (contextmanager(setter), True) if flag else (setter, False)
            for setter, flag in zip(setters, generator_flags)
        )

        def wrapped_pipe(instance, attrib, new_value):
            with ExitStack() as stack:
                rv = new_value

                for setter, is_generator_setter in prepared:
                    if is_generator_setter:
                        rv = stack.enter_context(setter(instance, attrib, rv))
                    else:
                        rv = setter(instance, attrib, rv)

                yield rv

        wrapped_pipe.__attrs_setter_is_generator__ = True
    else:

        def wrapped_pipe(instance, attrib, new_value):
            rv = new_value

            for setter in setters:
                rv = setter(instance, attrib, rv)

            return rv

        wrapped_pipe.__attrs_setter_is_generator__ = False

    return wrapped_pipe

.. _on-setattr-generators:

Generator hooks
---------------

The *on_setattr* arguments of `attrs.define`, `attrs.field`, `attr.s`, and
`attr.ib` accept generator functions as well as regular callables.
A generator hook receives the instance, attribute, and proposed value.
It must yield exactly once: the yielded value is assigned, and the generator
then resumes.
These hooks do not run during initialization.

Generator hooks follow the protocol of `contextlib.contextmanager`:
exceptions from assignment are thrown into the generator, and a generator
that yields zero or multiple times raises `RuntimeError`.
An exception raised after assignment does not undo the assignment.

When composed using `attrs.setters.pipe` or an *on_setattr* list, each hook's
returned or yielded value becomes the next hook's input.
Generators resume in reverse order after assignment.
A failure in a later hook is thrown into active generators.

.. versionadded:: 25.4.0

## Running code before and after assignment

An `on_setattr` generator hook yields the value to assign and resumes after
assignment. It must yield exactly once. Initialization does not run the hook.

```pycon
>>> from attrs import define
>>> changes = []
>>> def record_change(instance, attribute, value):
...     previous = getattr(instance, attribute.name)
...     yield value
...     changes.append((attribute.name, previous, value))
...
>>> @define(on_setattr=record_change)
... class Counter:
...     value: int = 0
...
>>> counter = Counter()
>>> counter.value = 3
>>> changes
[('value', 0, 3)]
```

Use `try`/`finally` around `yield` when cleanup must also run if assignment
fails. Exceptions raised after `yield` do not roll back an assignment.

The `on_setattr` hooks accepted by `attrs.define()`, `attrs.field()`, `attr.s()`, and `attr.ib()` can now be generator functions.
They must yield exactly once, yielding the value to assign, and resume after assignment.
Generator hooks can also be composed using `attrs.setters.pipe()` or lists of hooks.

If no exception is raised, the attribute is set to the return value
            of the callable.

            A generator function must yield exactly once. Its yielded value
            is assigned to the attribute, after which the generator resumes.
            Code before the yield observes the previous value; code after the
            yield observes the assigned value. An exception raised after
            assignment does not undo the assignment. Generator hooks follow
            the exception-handling rules of `contextlib.contextmanager`.

            If a list of callables is passed, they're automatically wrapped in
            an `attrs.setters.pipe`. Generator hooks resume in reverse order

def test_generator_on_setattr():
    """
    Generator hooks surround assignment and are not run during initialization.
    """
    import pytest

    from attrs import define, field

    for slots in (False, True):
        for attribute_hook in (False, True):
            events = []

            def hook(instance, attribute, value):
                events.append(("before", attribute.name, instance.value))
                yield value * 2
                events.append(("after", attribute.name, instance.value))

            @define(
                slots=slots,
                on_setattr=None if attribute_hook else hook,
            )
            class Example:
                value: int = field(
                    on_setattr=hook if attribute_hook else None
                )

            instance = Example(1)
            assert events == []

            instance.value = 3
            assert instance.value == 6
            assert events == [
                ("before", "value", 1),
                ("after", "value", 6),
            ]

            # Detection is performed when building the class.
            from unittest.mock import patch

            with patch(
                "attr.setters._is_generator",
                side_effect=AssertionError("unexpected detection"),
            ):
                instance.value = 4

            assert instance.value == 8


def test_generator_on_setattr_requires_one_yield():
    """
    Missing and extra yields raise with context-manager semantics.
    """
    import pytest

    from attrs import define

    def no_yield(instance, attribute, value):
        return
        yield  # pragma: no cover

    def two_yields(instance, attribute, value):
        yield value
        yield value

    for hook, message, expected in (
        (no_yield, "generator didn't yield", 1),
        (two_yields, "generator didn't stop", 2),
    ):

        @define(on_setattr=hook)
        class Example:
            value: int

        instance = Example(1)
        with pytest.raises(RuntimeError, match=message):
            instance.value = 2

        assert instance.value == expected


def test_generator_on_setattr_failure_after_assignment():
    """
    Exceptions after the yield do not roll back assignment.
    """
    import pytest

    from attrs import define

    def hook(instance, attribute, value):
        yield value
        raise ValueError("after assignment")

    @define(on_setattr=hook)
    class Example:
        value: int

    instance = Example(1)
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="after assignment"):
        instance.value = 2

    assert instance.value == 2

## Running code before and after assignment

An `on_setattr` hook can be a generator function that yields exactly once.
The yielded value becomes the attribute's new value.
The generator then resumes, allowing it to observe the completed assignment.
Hooks do not run during initialization.

```{doctest}
>>> from attrs import define
>>> changes = []
>>> def record_change(instance, attribute, value):
...     previous = getattr(instance, attribute.name)
...     yield value * 2
...     changes.append((previous, getattr(instance, attribute.name)))
...
>>> @define(on_setattr=record_change)
... class Counter:
...     value: int
...
>>> counter = Counter(1)
>>> counter.value = 3
>>> counter.value
6
>>> changes
[(1, 6)]
```

Generator hooks follow the rules of `contextlib.contextmanager`:
they must yield exactly once, and exceptions from assignment are raised at the yield.
An exception raised after assignment does not restore the previous value.
When hooks are composed using `attrs.setters.pipe` or an `on_setattr` list,
they run in order before assignment and resume in reverse order afterward.

`on_setattr` hooks now accept generator functions that yield exactly once.
The yielded value is assigned to the attribute before the generator resumes, allowing hooks to run code before and after assignment.
Generator hooks can also be composed using `attrs.setters.pipe` or a list of hooks.

On Python 3.13 and later, attrs classes support [`copy.replace()`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/copy.html#copy.replace):

```python
import copy

from attrs import define


@define(frozen=True)
class Point:
    x: int
    y: int


point = Point(1, 2)
moved = copy.replace(point, y=42)

assert Point(1, 42) == moved

```

Like `attrs.evolve()`, `copy.replace()` creates a new instance by calling the initializer, so converters and validators run again. It also works with frozen classes. Values of unchanged attributes are reused without being copied.

Changes use initializer parameter names, including aliases, rather than attribute names. Unknown parameter names raise `TypeError`.

attrs generates the `__replace__` method used by `copy.replace()` unless the class already defines one. On earlier Python versions, use `attrs.evolve()`.

import reprlib


def _is_dataclass_repr(obj: object) -> bool:
    """Check if an instance of a dataclass contains the default repr.

    Args:
        obj (object): A dataclass instance.

    Returns:
        bool: True if the default repr is used, False if there is a custom repr.
    """
    # Digging in to a lot of internals here
    # Catching all exceptions in case something is missing on a non CPython implementation
    try:
        repr_method = obj.__repr__
        filename = repr_method.__code__.co_filename
        if filename == dataclasses.__file__:
            return True
        # Python 3.13 uses reprlib.recursive_repr to wrap the generated repr.
        # Check the wrapped function too, so custom recursive reprs are preserved.
        return (
            filename == reprlib.__file__
            and repr_method.__wrapped__.__code__.co_filename == "<string>"
        )
    except Exception:  # pragma: no coverage
        return False

def test_is_dataclass_repr_default():

    from rich.pretty import _is_dataclass_repr, pretty_repr

    @dataclass

    example = Example(1)
    assert _is_dataclass_repr(example)
    assert pretty_repr(example, expand_all=True) == "Example(\n    value=1\n)"

from itertools import islice
from types import TracebackType
from typing import Iterator, Optional, Tuple


# Line numbers are one-based; columns are zero-based UTF-8 byte offsets.
TracebackPosition = Tuple[int, int, int, int]
SyntaxRange = Tuple[Tuple[int, int], Tuple[int, int]]


def get_traceback_positions(
    traceback: Optional[TracebackType],
) -> Iterator[Optional[TracebackPosition]]:
    """Yield an optional instruction range for every traceback frame."""
    while traceback is not None:
        position: Optional[TracebackPosition] = None
        co_positions = getattr(traceback.tb_frame.f_code, "co_positions", None)
        if co_positions is not None and traceback.tb_lasti >= 0:
            # CPython instructions occupy two-byte code units, including caches.
            instruction = traceback.tb_lasti // 2
            raw_position = next(
                islice(co_positions(), instruction, instruction + 1), None
            )
            if raw_position is not None:
                start_line, end_line, start_column, end_column = raw_position
                if (
                    start_line is not None
                    and end_line is not None
                    and start_column is not None
                    and end_column is not None
                ):
                    position = (
                        start_line,
                        start_column,
                        end_line,
                        end_column,
                    )
        yield position
        traceback = traceback.tb_next


def get_syntax_range(
    source: str, position: TracebackPosition
) -> Optional[SyntaxRange]:
    """Convert an instruction range to Syntax's character-based coordinates."""
    start_line, start_column, end_line, end_column = position
    lines = source.splitlines()
    if not (
        1 <= start_line <= end_line <= len(lines)
        and start_column >= 0
        and end_column >= 0
    ):
        return None

    start_bytes = lines[start_line - 1].encode("utf-8")
    end_bytes = lines[end_line - 1].encode("utf-8")
    if start_column > len(start_bytes) or end_column > len(end_bytes):
        return None

    try:
        start = (start_line, len(start_bytes[:start_column].decode("utf-8")))
        end = (end_line, len(end_bytes[:end_column].decode("utf-8")))
    except UnicodeDecodeError:
        return None

    return (start, end) if start < end else None

def _get_instruction_range(traceback: TracebackType) -> Optional[_InstructionRange]:
    """Get one-based lines and zero-based character columns for an instruction."""
    code = traceback.tb_frame.f_code
    co_positions = getattr(code, "co_positions", None)
    if co_positions is None or traceback.tb_lasti < 0:
        return None

    # co_positions includes inline cache entries; bytecode uses two-byte units.
    position = next(
        islice(co_positions(), traceback.tb_lasti // 2, None), None
    )
    if position is None:
        return None
    start_line, end_line, start_column, end_column = position
    if (
        start_line is None
        or end_line is None
        or start_column is None
        or end_column is None
    ):
        return None
    if start_line < 1 or end_line < start_line:
        return None
    if start_column < 0 or end_column < 0:
        return None

    # Python reports UTF-8 byte offsets, whereas Syntax uses character offsets.
    columns = []
    for lineno, byte_column in (
        (start_line, start_column),
        (end_line, end_column),
    ):
        source = linecache.getline(code.co_filename, lineno)
        if not source:
            return None
        encoded = source.encode("utf-8")
        if byte_column > len(encoded):
            return None
        try:
            column = len(encoded[:byte_column].decode("utf-8"))
        except UnicodeDecodeError:
            return None
        columns.append(column)

    start = (start_line, columns[0])
    end = (end_line, columns[1])
    return (start, end) if start < end else None

    def highlight_regex(
        self,
        re_highlight: Union[str, Pattern[str]],
        style: Optional[Union[GetStyleCallable, StyleType]] = None,
        *,
        style_prefix: str = "",
    ) -> int:
        """Highlight text with a regular expression, where group names are
        translated to styles.

        Args:
            re_highlight (Union[str, Pattern[str]]): A regular expression string or compiled pattern.
            style (Union[GetStyleCallable, StyleType]): Optional style to apply to whole match, or a callable
                which accepts the matched text and returns a style. Defaults to None.
            style_prefix (str, optional): Optional prefix to add to style group names.

        Returns:
            int: Number of regex matches
        """
        count = 0
        append_span = self._spans.append
        _Span = Span
        plain = self.plain
        for match in re.finditer(re_highlight, plain):
            get_span = match.span
            if style:
                start, end = get_span()
                match_style = style(plain[start:end]) if callable(style) else style
                if match_style is not None and end > start:
                    append_span(_Span(start, end, match_style))

            count += 1
            for name in match.groupdict().keys():
                start, end = get_span(name)
                if start != -1 and end > start:
                    append_span(_Span(start, end, f"{style_prefix}{name}"))
        return count

    import re

    pattern = re.compile(r"(?P<word>hello)(?: (?P<suffix>world))?", re.IGNORECASE)

        Span(6, 11, "test.suffix"),

    import re

    text = Text("RED blue")
    pattern = re.compile(r"red|blue", re.IGNORECASE)

    def get_style(matched_text: str) -> str:
        return matched_text.lower()

    count = text.highlight_regex(pattern, style=get_style)

from io import StringIO

import pytest

from rich.console import Console
from rich.traceback import Traceback


@pytest.mark.parametrize("attribute", ["__cause__", "__context__"])
@pytest.mark.parametrize("cycle_length", [1, 2, 3])
def test_exception_chain_cycle(attribute: str, cycle_length: int) -> None:
    exceptions = [ValueError(str(index)) for index in range(cycle_length)]
    for index, exception in enumerate(exceptions):
        setattr(exception, attribute, exceptions[(index + 1) % cycle_length])

    trace = Traceback.extract(ValueError, exceptions[0], None)

    assert [stack.exc_value for stack in trace.stacks] == [
        str(index) for index in range(cycle_length)
    ]
    output = StringIO()
    Console(file=output, width=80).print(Traceback(trace))
    assert "ValueError: 0" in output.getvalue()

import sys

import pytest

from rich.console import Console
from rich.traceback import Traceback


@pytest.mark.parametrize("attribute", ["__cause__", "__context__"])
@pytest.mark.parametrize("self_reference", [False, True])
def test_cyclic_exception_chain(attribute: str, self_reference: bool) -> None:
    first = ValueError("first")
    second = first if self_reference else ValueError("second")
    setattr(first, attribute, second)
    setattr(second, attribute, first)

    trace = Traceback.extract(type(first), first, None)

    assert [stack.exc_value for stack in trace.stacks] == (
        ["first"] if self_reference else ["first", "second"]
    )

def test_exception_group_cycle(attribute: str) -> None:
    child = ValueError("child")
    group = ExceptionGroup("group", [child])
    setattr(child, attribute, group)

    trace = Traceback.extract(type(group), group, None)

    assert len(trace.stacks) == 1
    children = trace.stacks[0].exceptions
    assert len(children) == 1
    assert [stack.exc_value for stack in children[0].stacks] == ["child"]

@pytest.mark.skipif(sys.version_info < (3, 11), reason="Requires exception groups")
def test_repeated_exception_in_sibling_groups() -> None:
    child = ValueError("shared child")
    left = ExceptionGroup("left", [child])
    right = ExceptionGroup("right", [child])
    group = ExceptionGroup("outer", [left, right])

    trace = Traceback.extract(type(group), group, None)

    branches = trace.stacks[0].exceptions
    assert len(branches) == 2
    for branch in branches:
        children = branch.stacks[0].exceptions
        assert len(children) == 1
        assert [stack.exc_value for stack in children[0].stacks] == ["shared child"]

Interactive mode
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

Rich automatically detects whether the console supports interactive output, such as animated progress displays. Set the ``TTY_INTERACTIVE`` environment variable to ``1`` to enable interactive mode or ``0`` to disable it. Other values, including an empty value, leave automatic detection enabled.

An explicit ``force_interactive`` argument to ``Console`` takes precedence over ``TTY_INTERACTIVE``. This environment variable does not change terminal or color detection.

    for segment in labels:

def test_inspect_unusual_qualname():
    from io import StringIO

    from rich import inspect
    from rich._inspect import Inspect
    from rich.console import Console

    class Callable:
        def __init__(self, qualname):
            self.__qualname__ = qualname

        def __call__(self):
            pass

    for qualname in (None, 42, b"callable", object()):
        obj = Callable(qualname)
        inspector = Inspect(obj)

        signature = inspector._get_signature("", obj)
        assert signature is not None
        assert signature.plain == "def ():"

        # Attribute names take precedence over unusual callable metadata.
        signature = inspector._get_signature("method", obj)
        assert signature is not None
        assert signature.plain == "def method():"

        output = StringIO()
        console = Console(file=output, width=80, color_system=None)
        inspect(obj, console=console, title="Callable", docs=False)
        assert "def ():" in output.getvalue()

            pass

# Automatic HEAD handling

Register the middleware before routing:

```go
e.Pre(middleware.AutoHandleHEAD())
```

A HEAD request that returns HTTP 405 is dispatched again as GET. The fallback preserves response headers and status and discards the response body. Explicit HEAD handlers otherwise take precedence. Missing routes continue to return HTTP 404.

The fallback runs the middleware chain again, and the GET handler observes the GET method. An explicit HEAD handler returning HTTP 405 also triggers fallback. Responses that have already been committed are never retried.

This implementation was drafted from the supplied excerpts; compilation and tests could not be run. It assumes the repository exposes `Context.Echo()`, `Context.Response()`, and the `github.com/labstack/echo/v5` module path.

.. Add to the uv_cancel() documentation:

    On Linux, filesystem requests submitted through io_uring can be cancelled
    when the kernel supports synchronous io_uring cancellation (Linux 6.0 or
    newer). If cancellation is unavailable or the operation can no longer be
    cancelled, this function returns ``UV_EBUSY``. Successful cancellation is
    delivered through the request's normal callback with ``UV_ECANCELED``;
    the request must remain valid until that callback runs.

.. note::
    On Linux, cancellation of filesystem requests submitted through io_uring
    requires Linux 6.0 or newer. On older kernels, :c:func:`uv_cancel` returns
    ``UV_EBUSY`` for these requests. Successfully cancelled requests still invoke
    their callbacks through the event loop, with ``UV_ECANCELED`` as the result.

/* Add alongside the filesystem test declarations. */
#ifdef __linux__
TEST_DECLARE(fs_cancel_read)
#endif

/* Add inside TASK_LIST_START, alongside the filesystem test entries. */
#ifdef __linux__
  TEST_ENTRY(fs_cancel_read)
#endif

On Linux, cancellation of filesystem requests submitted through io_uring
requires kernel support for synchronous cancellation (Linux 6.0 or newer).
If that operation is unavailable, :c:func:`uv_cancel` returns ``UV_EBUSY``.
Successful cancellation leaves callback delivery to the event loop; the request
must remain valid until its callback runs.
